$comment: PERIOD entity grammar — THE single source of truth for every time-range expression the system must understand. Consumed by: (1) generateFromSpec.ts entity fillers, (2) the QA scenario builder (src/knowledge/qa/), (3) the app's TemporalResolver test suite (WealthPilot utils/ai/nlp/resolvers/). Any period expression not representable here is out of contract. resolver_status/generator_status record CURRENT support as of 2026-07-18 — 'missing' entries are the implementation backlog, not aspirations. DATE vs PERIOD boundary rule: DATE is a POINT (a single day: 'yesterday', 'on Monday', 'June 5'); PERIOD is a RANGE ('last week', 'May', 'Q2'). A surface form must appear in exactly ONE of the two grammars — the previous overlap ('last week' in both DATE and PERIOD fillers) taught the NER head contradictory tags for identical text.

categories.meaning: The current unit, as a range.
The last/past N units as one contiguous range. THIS IS A SUMMARY RANGE, NOT A COMPARISON — see ambiguity_rules.
numeric_range with the count spelled as a word. Identical semantics to numeric_range.
A named calendar month of the current (or most recent past) year.
A named month of an explicit year.
A calendar quarter, absolute (Q1–Q4) or relative (this/last quarter).
categories.resolver_status: supported (Q1-Q4, this/last quarter, 'quarter before last'; tested)

categories.meaning: Half of a calendar year. H1 = Jan–Jun, H2 = Jul–Dec.
surface_forms: first six months of the year

categories.meaning: A whole year, absolute or relative.
categories.resolver_status: supported (explicit year, for-the-year; fiscal-year at LOW confidence by design; tested)

categories.meaning: From the start of the current unit until today.
Non-specific recency. MUST resolve to low confidence and trigger a default window or clarification — never a guessed exact range.
categories.resolver_status: supported (falls through to UNKNOWN, which is the correct behavior)

comparison.$comment: Comparison ROLES (period1 vs period2) are NOT model labels. The NER head tags every period span as PERIOD; a deterministic role assigner in the app (EntityExtractor) orders spans into period1/period2 using these markers. implicit_second: comparative phrasings with ONE explicit period imply the current unit as period1. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-18: WealthPilot utils/ai/nlp/resolvers/periodRoles.ts (assignPeriodRoles, 12 tests) — wired via EntityExtractor.applySpanExtras (TFJS spans path) AND FinanceDispatcher single-period derivation (LLM path); R4 enforced by an orchestrator clarification gate.
role_rules: Two PERIOD spans + a marker between them: span BEFORE marker = period1, span AFTER = period2.
Two PERIOD spans, no marker: first span in token order = period1.
One PERIOD span + an implicit_comparative_cue: period1 = current unit of the found span's granularity, period2 = the found span.
Zero PERIOD spans on a COMPARISON taskType: DO NOT default silently — emit needsClarification (fixes SpendingEngine.ts:130's invented 'last month').

ambiguity_rules: 'spending last two months' (no comparison verb/marker) = ONE numeric_range SUMMARY.
'compare last two months' / 'last month vs the month before' = COMPARISON of two adjacent months. The verb/marker decides; the taskType head must be trained on minimal pairs (see QA class T5).

A bare month name ('May') in a comparison context ('May vs June') is absolute_month; the SAME token in 'spent 500 in May' is also absolute_month — but 'may' as a modal verb ('it may help') must stay O-tagged. Include modal-verb negative patterns in training.
